simulate.title: Simulation
simulate.subtitle: Closed-loop vehicle dynamics: trajectory, controllers, actuators and vehicle model.
simulate.modelTip: Kinematic: no tire slip. Linear/nonlinear single track: lateral dynamics. Double track: roll and wheel spin. Multibody: heave, pitch, unsprung masses. Neural: trained surrogate.
simulate.lateralTip: Steers the vehicle along the reference path.
simulate.muTip: 1.0 dry asphalt, about 0.5 wet, about 0.2 snow.
simulate.solverTip: RK4 is accurate at the default step; Euler and Heun are for comparisons.
simulate.durationHint: 0 = until the end of the maneuver

models.title: Neural models
models.subtitle: Train a neural surrogate of the vehicle dynamics or a network that proposes the planned trajectory, or connect your own model. Every model is compared with its teacher before you use it.
models.externalInfo: External model: no training metrics. Use the closed-loop comparison below to validate it.

evaluate.title: Closed-loop validation
evaluate.text: Runs the same maneuver with the same controllers twice: with the physics teacher and with the neural model.

kindHint.vehicle_dynamics: A network that replaces the vehicle model in simulations.
kindHint.trajectory_planner: A network that proposes the trajectory of each planning cycle; the Werling planner verifies it.

trainForm.demonstrationsTip: Planning cycles of the Werling planner in random situations (roads, speeds, lane offsets, objects). Collecting them takes most of the time: about 25 ms each.
trainForm.title: Train a surrogate
trainForm.text: The network learns the accelerations of a physics model from Monte Carlo samples of the driving envelope.
trainForm.teacherTip: The model whose exact derivatives provide the training data.
trainForm.samplesTip: More samples improve accuracy; 20 000 take a few seconds.
trainForm.hiddenHint: Neurons per layer, comma separated, e.g. 64, 64
trainForm.name: Name

howPlanner.text: The network learns which trajectory the Werling planner selects: the end offset and end time of the lateral motion and the end speed and end time of the longitudinal motion. In every cycle the planner builds only the candidates next to this proposal and checks them with the same restrictions and collision check as always.
howPlanner.validation: After training, the guided planner and the Werling planner drive the same held-out situations. If no candidate next to the proposal is valid, or the best one lies on the border of the local set, the cycle uses the complete Werling search.

how.title: How the surrogate works
how.text: The planar kinematics stay exact; only the accelerations come from the network. The model is then a drop-in replacement of the vehicle model in every simulation.
how.validation: After training, the test-set R² and RMSE per output are shown, and a closed-loop comparison checks the error that matters for planning.

parking.title: Parking
parking.subtitle: Plan and drive a parking maneuver: parallel, perpendicular or angled spots, forward or in reverse, for any steering and drive configuration.

steeringHint.front: Conventional car: the rear axle moves without side slip and is the planning reference point.
steeringHint.rear: Only the rear wheels steer (like a forklift): the front axle is the reference point and the rear swings out in turns.
steeringHint.counter: Rear wheels steer opposite to the front: smaller turning circle, reference point between the axles. Production rear-axle steering at low speed.
steeringHint.in_phase: Rear wheels steer like the front: larger turning circle, the vehicle moves more sideways. Meant for high speed; needs more space for parking.

parking.steeringTip: Which wheels steer decides where the vehicle turns about (instantaneous center of rotation) and how small its turning circle is.
parking.layoutTip: Which wheels are driven decides the traction on slopes and low friction (load on the driven axle times friction).
parking.gapHint: Empty = vehicle length + 1.8 m; + 1.4 m is a tight spot with many moves
parking.ratioTip: tan(rear angle) / tan(front angle): negative = counter-phase, positive = in-phase.
parking.slopeTip: Positive = uphill in the driving direction of the street.

empty.title: Choose a parking task
empty.text: The planner searches a drivable path into the spot (Hybrid A* with Reeds-Shepp curves), then a controller drives it on a low-speed vehicle model.

parking.failed: The planner found no path into this spot.
parking.viewHint: Solid: forward, dashed: reverse. Gray: curb and walls, orange: parked vehicles, green: target spot.
parking.geometryInfo: Turning radius of the reference point {{r}} m · reference point {{p}} m ahead of the rear axle · max. steering front {{f}}°, rear {{rr}}°

conditions.label: Conditions
conditions.realistic: Realistic (double track, sensor noise, 0.1 s latency)
conditions.harsh: Ice and poor sensors (friction 0.3, 0.2 s latency)

hint.ideal: The plant is the controller's own design model and every measurement is exact. Good for understanding the algorithms; tracking is almost perfect.
hint.realistic: Double-track vehicle with load transfer and tire saturation; objects and the own position are measured with noise and arrive 0.1 s late.
hint.wet: As realistic, on a wet road. The planner does not know the friction: watch the lateral acceleration it asks for.
hint.harsh: Low friction and poor sensors. Expect missions to fail; that is the point of this preset.

control.title: Controller lab
control.subtitle: Run several tracking controllers on the same path and vehicle, compare how well they follow it, and see how each term of a control law contributes at any moment.

pathHints.lane_change: 3.5 m to the left over 50 m.
pathHints.double_lane_change: To the left and back, 40 m each.
pathHints.curve_entry: Straight, then a 60 m radius with a 20 m transition.
pathHints.straight: Use it with a start offset or a side force to see the pure reaction of the loop.

control.plantTip: The model the controller drives. The design model is the simplest; the double-track and multibody models add load transfer, tire saturation and roll.
control.offsetHint: Positive: to the left of the path
control.gustHint: A lateral force at the center of gravity for 0.5 s, like a wind gust. 3000 N is a strong gust for a sedan.

empty.text: Pick controllers and a path. The lab drives each controller through the same maneuver and shows errors, steering and the control law.

result.title: Comparison
result.text: Vehicle model: {{plant}} · friction {{mu}} · {{speed}} km/h. Click a row to see its control law below.

kpi.note: Settled: the lateral error stays below 5 cm from this time on.

law.title: Control law
law.text: The formula of the selected controller and the value of each term at the time of the slider.
law.noTerms: This controller reports no separate terms.

explain.pure_pursuit: Pure Pursuit steers along a circle from the rear axle to a point on the path that lies the look-ahead distance L_d ahead. A long look-ahead is smooth but cuts corners; a short one follows closely but oscillates.
explain.stanley: Stanley looks at the front axle. It aligns the wheels with the path (heading term), steers toward the path in proportion to the lateral error and inversely to the speed (feedback), adds the steering angle the curvature needs (feedforward) and damps the yaw rate.
explain.lqr: The LQR uses the linear single-track model in error coordinates. The gain K minimizes a weighted sum of errors and steering effort and is recomputed for each speed; the feedforward holds the vehicle on a curve without error.
explain.mpc: The MPC plans the steering rate over a horizon by solving an optimization with the error model and limits on angle and rate, applies the first part of the plan and plans again.
explain.werling_bilevel: The Werling controller inverts the nonlinear single-track model so that the lateral error follows a chosen linear second-order equation. At low speed it switches to a kinematic law; a large deviation triggers a re-initialization of the planner.
